_note: Copy guidance for the questionnaire components (registry item vois-questionnaire, default strings in lib/questionnaire/copy.ts). Moved here from righter/data/components.json in vois-patterns 1.23.2. Reviewed with the righter skill when a question is added.

components.name: Prefill badge and source line
components.when_to_use: A field or answer holds a value the user did not type this session: from a profile, a link, an earlier answer, or an AI guess.
components.golden_rule: Say where the value came from, and make it easy to change.
rules: Badge: 2 to 5 words, sentence case, no period. Name the source in plain words
Source line: under 60 characters. Say 'Source:' then where it came from
Never show a confidence percentage. Use a word such as Likely, or show the source instead
After the user edits, the badge becomes 'Edited by you'
'Not me' clears every prefilled identity field in one tap
Undo message: say what was cleared, with one Undo action
When two sources disagree, show both values and let the user pick

variants.name: Sources disagree
variants.sentence_construction: Your profile says X. Last time you said Y.

components.name: Selection limit and count
components.when_to_use: A multiple choice question has a minimum, a maximum, or an exclusive option.
components.golden_rule: State the rule before the user answers. Explain every disabled option.
rules: Helper states the limit before the answer: 'Select up to 3'
Count updates live: '2 of 3 selected'
At the max, say why options are disabled and how to free one
Exclusive option: say it clears the others
Never say 'invalid selection'. Say what to do

variants.name: Max reached
variants.sentence_construction: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.
examples: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.

variants.name: Exclusive
variants.sentence_construction: Choosing X clears your other choices
examples: Choosing 'None of these' clears your other choices.

variants.name: Error
variants.sentence_construction: Select at least N. You selected M.

good: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.

components.name: Availability check
components.when_to_use: The system checks whether a value is free or valid on the server, such as a name, handle, or code.
components.golden_rule: Say what is happening, what the result means, and what to do next.
rules: Checking: 2 to 3 words, shown only if the check takes more than a moment
Available: say so in 1 to 2 words. Do not celebrate
Taken: say it is taken and suggest the next step. Do not blame
Cannot check: say the check failed and that the user can continue
Never reveal whether an account exists for a sensitive value

variants.name: Cannot check
variants.sentence_construction: Couldn't check right now. We'll check again when you submit.
examples: Couldn't check right now. We'll check again when you submit.

bad: Oops! Someone beat you to it!

components.name: One-time code and resend
components.when_to_use: The user enters a one-time code and may ask for another.
components.golden_rule: Tell them where the code went and when they can ask again.
rules: Say where the code was sent without showing the full address or number
Show the wait as a plain countdown
Resend is a button once the wait ends
A wrong code says the code did not match and what to do. It does not say how close it was
An expired code says it expired and offers a new one

variants.name: Sent
variants.sentence_construction: We sent a code to + masked target

variants.name: Wrong code
variants.sentence_construction: That code didn't match. Check it and try again.
examples: That code didn't match. Check it and try again.

variants.name: Expired
variants.sentence_construction: That code expired. Send a new one.
examples: That code expired. Send a new one.

bad: Please wait before requesting another code

components.name: Saved state and drafts
components.when_to_use: A long form or questionnaire saves answers, restores a draft, or a link would replace a saved draft.
components.golden_rule: Never use a modal to say something was saved.
rules: Saved state is a quiet inline word, not a toast or modal
Failed save says it did not save and offers Retry
Save and finish later states how long the draft is kept
A link that would overwrite a saved draft asks before it does
Name both choices with verbs

variants.name: Finish later
variants.sentence_construction: We'll keep your answers for N days.
examples: We'll keep your answers for 30 days.

variants.name: Overwrite warning
variants.title: You have a saved draft
variants.sentence_construction: Continue the saved draft or start with the link's answers?

bad: Your progress has been successfully saved!

components.name: Questionnaire errors
components.when_to_use: The respondent presses Next and one or more questions fail a check.
components.golden_rule: Say what to fix on each question, in the place it needs fixing.
rules: Banner: count the problems, then link to each
Inline error: say what to do and what happened. Under 60 characters
Required is a plain word, not an asterisk alone
Never say 'invalid'. Never blame the respondent

variants.name: Too few
variants.sentence_construction: Select at least N. You selected M.

components.name: Progress and review
components.when_to_use: A questionnaire shows where the respondent is, a review screen, or a confirmation.
components.golden_rule: Honest counts, and say what happens after Submit.
rules: Progress text: 'Question n of N' or 'Section n of N'. Never a bare percentage
Review screen title says what to do: Review your answers
Confirmation says it worked, what was received, and what happens next
Skipped-by-logic answers show as removed on Review

variants.name: Confirmation
variants.sentence_construction: Title: what worked. Body: what we got and what happens next.
examples: We'll use them to plan the next release. You don't need to do anything else.

components.name: Rank prompts
components.when_to_use: The respondent ranks items by dragging, or with the up and down buttons.
components.golden_rule: Say how to rank, and say what changed after every move.
rules: Helper says how: press and hold, then drag, or use the arrows
Say the limit when it is the top N
Each move is announced in full: item, new position, total
Never make drag the only way

variants.name: Helper
variants.sentence_construction: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top N count.
examples: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top 3 count.

variants.name: Position
variants.sentence_construction: Item, moved to position n of N
examples: Battery life, moved to position 2 of 6

variants.name: Cutoff
variants.sentence_construction: Your top N end here. Items below are not ranked.
examples: Your top 3 end here. Items below are not ranked.

good: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top 3 count.

components.name: Poll and quiz results
components.when_to_use: After a respondent answers a choice question, the screen shows how others answered, and in a quiz which option is correct.
components.golden_rule: Say what the numbers are out of, and say the result in words, not only in color.
rules: Mark the right option with the words 'Correct answer'. Mark the respondent's pick with 'Your answer'
Give the count in plain words: '1 vote', '42 votes'. Never 'votes: 42'
Under the minimum, say there are too few votes. Do not show a percent or count
For multi-select, say the percents add up to more than 100%
The announcement is one short sentence about this respondent's result. It does not list every option
Do not cheer or console. 'Not quite' is enough for a wrong answer

variants.name: Too few votes
variants.sentence_construction: Too few votes to show results yet.
examples: Too few votes to show results yet.

variants.name: Multi-select note
variants.sentence_construction: Each percent is out of everyone who answered. They add up to more than 100%.
examples: Each percent is out of everyone who answered. They add up to more than 100%.

variants.name: Announcement, wrong answer
variants.sentence_construction: Not quite. The correct answer is X.
examples: Not quite. The correct answer is 366. 62% of people chose it.

variants.name: Announcement, poll
variants.sentence_construction: Results are in. N people answered.

good: Not quite. The correct answer is 366.
